name: History and Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
description: Historical notions of intelligence; formalisation of ideas of computing; intelligence as computing and the birth of AI; relation to philosophical functionalism; early examples, role of symbols and logic; frame problem and its modern avatars; problem of induction and deeper epistemological questions; connectionism, its history and evolution; key debates and critiques -- Chinese room, Dreyfus attack, neural network systematicity, nature and role of representation; the idea of learning, innateness vs. adaptation, relation to rationalism-empiricism debates; hybrid approaches, cognitive architectures; agentic AI, notions of self and agency; nature and building blocks of reasoning, conceptions of rational machines; overview of AI ethics and capacity for moral decision-making; centrality of deep learning in modern AI and its implications for philosophical questions and future directions
